description.narrative: Strengthening and increasing road transport infrastructure and its reliability

The objectives of the Road Sector Development Program and Fourth Adaptable Program Loan Project for Ethiopia are to assist the Government in strengthening and increasing its road transport infrastructure and its reliability, and strengthening the institutional efficiency in road sector management. Three are three components to the project. The first component of the project is upgrading of federal link roads and related supervision services. This component comprises upgrading of two link roads from an existing gravel surface to asphalt surface, and one from an existing earth road to asphalt surface road as follows: (i) upgrading of Mekenajo-Dembi Dolo Link road sub-project (181 km asphalt concrete); (ii) upgrading of Welkite-Hosaina Link road sub-project (121 km asphalt concrete); (iii) upgrading of Ankober-Awash Arba Link road sub-project (89 km asphalt surface treatment); and (iv) construction supervision of these three roads including implementing the associated environmental, safety, and resettlement plans and mitigation of adverse social impacts, as well as sectional design review of Ankober-Awash Arba road. The second component of the project is Ethiopian Roads Authority (ERA) modernization/sector capacity building. This component various institutional strengthening/reform and capacity building activities will be undertaken, comprising: (i) preparatory study toward establishing a highway engineering research center: and (ii) technical advisory services (TA) to prepare and conduct Harmonized 'comprehensive capacity building'. ERA staff training will also be included. The third component of the project is network management studies. This component will be conducted comprising: (i) maintenance needs assessment and updating of road financing study; (ii) transport and poverty observatories (TPOs); and (iii) preparatory studies for the next phase of Road Sector Development Program (RSDP) and the Universal Rural Access Roads Program (URAP).

title.narrative: Road maintenance and financing needs for the coming 10 years projected (ETB million)

comment.narrative: The road financing study, completed in 2012, has produced a set of recommendations to diversify road fund revenues. Out of the many recommendations, as a first step, the Government has approved the revenue from vehicles registration to be part of the RF revenue starting from July 2015. It is estimated that the additional revenue will increase the RF collection by about 15%, bringing the total collection to ETB 2.1bl (US$100 mil equivalent), and is hoped that this additional resource will improve the ability of the RF to finance more roads, narrowing the demand gap for maintenance.

Roads in good and fair condition as a share of total classified roads

comment.narrative: Road in good and fair condition remains about 86% of the total classified road network, including rural roads which are being constructed under the Universal Rural Roads Access Program (URRAP). These roads constitutes about 48.5% (54,966km) of the network, while the roads under the federal and regional government constitute 51.5% (58,247), totaling 113,213 km.

Average travel time: Except Ankober-Awash Arba (89 km) which was dropped from the credit by the request of the Government, Wolkite-Hossaina (126km) and Mekenajo-Dembidolo (181km) are complete to asphalt road and opened for traffic. The average travel speed on these roads is currently about 60km per hour or1.0 min per km, down from 2.5-3.0 min per km (25--20 km per hr). The fgure in the previous ISR was 0.8min per km which means 75km per hr. This has now been correct to the current figure (1.0 min per km)   based on the latest information collected from ERA.

title.narrative: Comprehensive Capacity Building Program activities implemented

comment.narrative: The service includes training program to ERA staff and identifying training requirements to other professionals in the sector at large. Thus, most of the funds have already been used to train three ERA engineers overseas at MSc level; three at MPhil level (blended course), and for a consultancy service for a sector wide capacity needs assessment. The final report of the need assessment was submitted to ERA in May 2014. Based on the recommendations of the study, a comprehensive five years sector capacity building program is under implementation by ERA. The report has also been shard to Ministry of Transport for their actions. &nsp;

title.narrative: Comprehensive Capacity Building Program activities implemented
Comprehensive Capacity Building Program activities implemented

comment.narrative:
Out of the three roads designed to be constructed under the project, one (Ankober-Awash Arba 89km) was dropped from the project by the request of the Government, and hence not done under the project. However, the road is currently under construction through Government's own resources.
The other two roads: Wolkite-Hossaina (126 km) and Mekenajo-Dembidolo (181km), totaling 307 km are complete. Since Ankober- Awash Arba is formally dropped from the project, from implementatio perspective all the road components are complete.

comment.narrative:
With the submission of the last and final year (Year 4) report by end of December 2016, and subsequent workshop organized to stakeholders on May 2, 2017 to discuss the findings of the study, the service is considered as complete, and the report will be distributed to all stakeholders. Since TPO was a multiyear observatory study on the impact of road improvements on the socio-economic activity of people living along the corridor, it is believed that it provides information on changes resulted from the road investments and can also be used in future as an input for road investment analysis.
All four roads were monitoring for a period of four years.

Preparatory study for a Highway Engineering Research Center completed and implementation of agreed organizational option commenced

comment.narrative:
Preparatory for a Highway Research center was complete on 31 December 2012 with all deliverables submitted to ERA. by  2013.  ERA has already started implementing research program.
The Highway research center is now fully functional and, with the help of a consultant through the Bank's support, ERA has developed a five year business plan and identified six research areas to focus. The Bank is pleased to note that the Government is currently strengthening the research center with modern road laboratory equipment, research materials and new staff to bring it to acceptable level.
